description: Check a pulse job as a host returned it ({"request", "result"}, the result with its receipt): the receipt's signature, the program's digest against the request's text, and the request run again here with the result held to the one given field by field (the density matrix's digest among them), each difference named. A pulse run is the same bits on every platform, so a result that does not reproduce was not made from that request by this engine. Sealed with the service's key. Quote `verified` and the statement.
name: pulse_check

anyOf.description: A pulse answer as every host gives it (engine::pulse: pulse_schedule and pulse_check on both servers, wai-quantum pulse, POST /v1/pulse/*, the Studio): the request, and the result sealed in a job's form. A pulse program's schedule on frames, or a pulse job checked by running it again. A pulse run itself is a job (method pulse) and follows job-result.v1.json. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema). docs/pulse.md explains each.

A pulse program's schedule (pulse_schedule, wai-quantum pulse schedule, POST /v1/pulse/schedule): its frames and ports, every instruction at its sample, each waveform's samples, the gate calls, the reader's notes, and the digests a run binds.

calibration.description: What a pulse run's receipt binds of the program: the BLAKE3 of the control program's text, of its calibrations as written (every cal, defcal and defcalgrammar, joined by newlines), and of the schedule's JSON; a run adds the device's and the target snapshot's.

duration.description: The latest time of any frame, samples.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

carrier.description: The carrier's phase at the play's first sample, cycles in [0, 1).

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.
